title: Letters to Joel Spolsky: a satirical essay on ego, insecurity and chasing a big name
summary: A humorous series of fictional emails from Jason Cohen to Joel Spolsky, moving from a snarky rejection to groveling and then pestering follow-ups. It is satire, not a playbook, and offers little durable guidance on growth, pricing or building a business beyond a nod to Joel's influence and the idea of learning by copying.

principles.text: Learn by copying: borrowing the structure of work you admire is a legitimate way to create.
principles.quote: Good artists copy; great artists steal. (Said by Steve Jobs, stealing a quote from Pablo Picasso.)

principles.text: Writers whose ideas shaped how you hire, bootstrap, ship and run support are worth acknowledging openly.
principles.quote: As an entrepreneur, you've taught me everything from how to hire great people, how to think properly about bootstrapping, how new projects help you cope with burn-out, and even how to run tech support.
